text:
Alex: Heads up — seeing apiserver 5xx spikes and controller-manager OOM/restarts coinciding with the GPU node scale-up in us-west1, started ~10:12 UTC.
Maria: Yep noticed alerts. Apiserver latency jumped to 2s+ and leader election churned.
Thomas: Any recent infra changes around NAT or autoscaler configs?
Alex: We ramped +40 GPU nodes to satisfy a batch onboarding job. Autoscaler did burst add around 10:11.
SRE-Oncall: pulling logs now.
SRE-Oncall: apiserver log snippet: 
```
E1012 10:12:15.123456 1 httplog.go:123] http2: server: error reading preface from client 10.4.8.12: read tcp 10.0.5.3:443->10.4.8.12:53421: i/o timeout
W1012 10:12:16.234567 1 authentication.go:70] failed token review: dial tcp etcd-usw1:2379: i/o timeout
```
Maria: controller-manager logs show leaderElection reacquire loops + CrashLoopBackoff for a few replicas.
Alex: kubectl get pods -n kube-system shows many kube-proxy on new nodes Pending/CrashLoopBackoff? but mostly Running.
Thomas: suspect conntrack / SNAT exhaustion on the NAT gateway. When we add many GPU pods they open many ephemeral connections to control plane endpoints + metrics exporters.
SRE-Oncall: checking node conntrack: 
```
# on node gpu-42
$ sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
65528
$ sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 65536
```
SRE-Oncall: we were basically at the limit.
Maria: Oof. That explains the intermittent TCP read timeouts. New nodes suddenly create a ton of kubelet/metrics/health probes to apiserver and etcd.
Thomas: Any SNAT port metrics from the NAT?
SRE-Oncall: NAT SNAT ports exhausted on the edge pool for that region — logs show SNAT allocation fail + retries.
Alex: So packets drop, apiserver/etcd RPCs time out, leader election loses quorum, controller-manager restarts. Chain reaction.
Maria: Quick mitigation: drain newly added GPU nodes and cordon them to stop the spike. Can someone sequence that? @Thomas can you? :pray:
Thomas: On it — draining gpu-* nodes now: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-41 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl drain gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
DeployBot: [deploy] autoscaler-adjustment /commit/67423 triggered at 10:09 UTC
SRE-Oncall: Also increasing nf_conntrack_max as emergency patch on nodes to 262144. Patching via fleet script now.
Alex: Good. Longer-term we need to avoid hitting NAT limits: options - add more SNAT IPs, enable node-local SNAT, move control plane endpoints to private peering, or reduce ephemeral connections (kubelet scrape intervals, metrics sampling).
Maria: Cost note: adding more SNAT IPs / egress capacity isn't free. If this burst pattern repeats tradeoff between reserved GPU capacity vs repeated scale-bursts causing infra churn. Reserved capacity could smooth things and avoid sudden conntrack pressure.
Thomas: Agree. Also we can add API rate-limiting and increase apiserver --max-requests-inflight / throttling to protect control plane from a single region flood.
SRE-Oncall: Observability items: collect conntrack growth over the last 2 hours, SNAT port usage, new-node join logs, kubelet connection patterns. I'll drop a dashboard.
Alex: Action list: 1) drain/cordon new nodes (done in progress), 2) bump nf_conntrack_max on nodes (in progress), 3) add temporary extra SNAT IPs to edge pool (ops runbook), 4) revert autoscaler policy to slower ramp for GPU pools, 5) plan reserved capacity discussion with finance/product.
Maria: I'll open a ticket for reserved Dedicated GPU commit options and estimated monthly delta.
Thomas: After drains, let's watch apiserver latency / leader stability for 30m. If stable, we can add nodes slower.
SRE-Oncall: Patch applied to 12/15 new nodes; conntrack count dropped after evicting pods. apiserver 5xx rate down to baseline ~0.5/min.
Alex: Thanks team. Follow-ups: add a canary config for future scale-ups (stagger additions), consider node-local-proxy and reducing control-plane scrape frequency from metrics exporters on GPU nodes.
Maria: +1. I'll schedule a postmortem if alerts cross threshold again.
Thomas: Noted — also check kube-proxy conntrack settings and ensure conntrack helpers off for workloads that open many short connections.
SRE-Oncall: documenting steps we ran in the incident channel.
Alex: Closing here once the dashboard confirms stability for 1h. :thumbsup:
